_README: Published porosity + particle-density values per grain-size class, used
ONLY to ESTIMATE a baseline filterable volume at a membrane pore size no
real trial has calibrated (lib/baseline.ts's estimateBaselineVolume,
rebuild phase 10). Every real trial calibration still supersedes this
the moment one exists - see lib/trials.ts and HANDOFF.md rule 7.
WHY THIS EXISTS: data/trials.json's 10 real bench trials all used a
5 um filter, so every other pore size had no real calibration anchor at
all - a real, honest 'insufficient data'. But a UK-wide tool cannot wait
for a bench trial at every pore size at every site: it needs to infer,
to a stated degree, from geology and published literature - clearly
labelled as an estimate, not a measurement, and always superseded by
real data the moment it exists. This file is that literature input.
THE PHYSICS: Carman-Kozeny gives specific cake resistance as
proportional to (1-porosity) / (porosity^3 * particleDensity) - this is
what actually converts a particle-SHAPE term (already computed from the
PSD alone, no new assumption) into a true physical resistance. The real
trial-calibrated k constant (lib/baseline.ts) silently assumes the
AQUARIUM SOIL trial feed's own porosity/density applies to every site,
whatever its real character - this file corrects that by RATIO: how
much a site's own class differs from the trial feed's measured
silt-range particle size (d50 22-31 um across all 10 real trials, i.e.
genuinely silt-class by Wentworth, not an assumption). The apparatus
constants (filter area, pressure, Kozeny's own K constant, unit
conversions) are IDENTICAL for the trial feed and the new site and
cancel out of that ratio - so this file only needs porosity and density
per class, nothing else.
WHY THE RANGES ARE WIDE, ESPECIALLY FOR CLAY: porosity is itself
variable (packing, consolidation, flocculation state), and literature
confirms it - published sand porosity runs about 0.38-0.46 across real
studies; clay, because freshly suspended/flocculated fine sediment can
be far more open-structured than consolidated clay, runs anywhere from
about 0.47 (soil-hydrology tables, consolidated) to 0.9 (river-
modelling literature, freshly deposited cohesive sediment). This file
reports that real spread rather than picking one number and hiding the
uncertainty - it is the same reason data/screening-parameters.json's
flocDensityPenalty stays unmodelled: this project does not model floc
structure, so clay's estimate necessarily carries the most of that
unmodelled uncertainty, reflected honestly in how wide its range is.
Particle (mineral solid) density is held at one value, 2650 kg/m3,
across all three classes - this is standard quartz/feldspar density,
the dominant mineral in UK fluvial sediment at every grain size, and
common clay minerals (kaolinite ~2600, illite ~2750) sit close enough
to it that the difference is swamped by the porosity uncertainty above.
What genuinely differs for clay - a flocculated particle's much lower
EFFECTIVE density once it entrains water - is exactly the unmodelled
floc-density gap already named in data/screening-parameters.json, not
something this file invents a number for.
SOURCES (real, checked live via web search, not recalled from training):
sand porosity:  Comparative Study of Sand Porosity (marine sand,
average ~41.3%, review range 37.7-46.3% across packing
states), https://aquila.usm.edu/fac_pubs/8601
silt porosity:  Benthic sediment porosity survey, sand-to-mud gradient
(sand ~0.44, muddy sand ~0.55, sandy mud ~0.58),
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4530241/table/tab1
clay porosity:  Minnesota stormwater soil-property tables (consolidated
clay ~0.47-0.48), https://stormwater.pca.state.mn.us/index.php/Soil_water_storage_properties ;
high end (freshly deposited cohesive sediment, up to
0.9) from river-modelling guidance referenced in the
same search round - see HANDOFF.md for the full note.
Kozeny-Carman form + the real-cake-deviates-from-theory caveat:
Pressure Filtration Theory, https://www.911metallurgist.com/blog/pressure-filtration-theory/ ;
specific-resistance limits, https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/152237/1/processes-07-00746.pdf

sand.note: Tightly packed to loose, real published range for fluvial/marine sand - the most consistent of the three classes.

silt.note: Sand-to-mud gradient from a real benthic survey - silt sits between sand and clay, both in grain size and in porosity.

clay.note: The widest range of the three, honestly - consolidated clay soils sit near 0.47, but freshly suspended/flocculated river clay (the state that actually matters for a filter cake forming from suspended load) can be far more open, up to 0.9. This is this file's biggest source of estimate uncertainty.
